### Why the old test fails

The acquisition oracle treated intersections of `SVGTextElement.getBBox()` envelopes as intersections of visible text. Under the very small effective transforms, Chromium returns transform-dependent font-cell envelopes. These include unpainted font ascent/descent space and are larger than the natural-font envelope scaled into screen space. `getBoundingClientRect()` confirms that these *envelopes* really intersect in screen coordinates; this is not a mistaken omission of the camera transform. It does not prove that their painted glyph pixels overlap.

For example, `category:987` / “Number theory” has a natural 17px/600 title envelope of **20 world units** in height. In Course 12, its scaled natural height would be about **3.32063 CSS px**, whereas the reported transformed envelope is **4 CSS px**, or **24.091814 world units** after inverse scaling. In Project 180, it is again 4 CSS px, equivalent to **24.799570 world units** instead of 20. For Stage 2443's `category:1162` / “Computer”, the natural 21px/600 title envelope is 24 units high; scaling gives about **4.24316 CSS px**, but the transformed envelope is 5 CSS px, or **28.280775 world units**. These enlarged font envelopes intersect neighboring line/coverage envelopes, while their actual glyph silhouettes remain separate.

This interpretation is supported by direct painted-pixel tests at Fit All, rather than by the passing natural-zoom test alone:

1. Every one of the 646 pairs was independently rendered into aligned alpha silhouettes in Chromium using the exact effective screen matrix, font family, font size/weight, original x/y, fractional position and DPR. Both labels in every pair produced nonzero ink. **Zero shared nonzero-alpha pixels** were found, including all antialiased edge pixels; thresholds 32/255 and 64/255 were also zero. No threshold was raised to conceal a collision.
2. Native Chromium screenshots of the original SVG text elements, isolated without changing their positions, independently checked the worst envelope-area title→title and title→coverage case in each scope. The only probe changes were temporary visibility isolation and white-on-black paint, preserving fonts, coordinates, transforms and geometry. All six cases have **zero shared painted pixels**. Same-label positive controls produce nonzero shared pixels, so the detector does not pass blank masks.
3. Natural-size text envelopes do not intersect for any reported pair or elsewhere in the six focused scopes. Their ordinary world geometry and native line spacing are separate from the tiny-scale font-cell envelopes.

Native screenshot probes were small temporary glyph crops outside Git, not a screenshot matrix or new review captures. The six worst-pair results are:

### Involved generic CSS and optical rules

The following rules apply to every scope and are unchanged:

- **R1 Category title:** `layout.js` measures full text, Category fonts 17 / used-root fonts 21 / presentation font 28, with `line = font × 1.3`; Category title weight 600, presentation 650. `app.js` emits all full wrapped lines at x=22 and y=`8 + font + i × line`. Geometry is freshly local and card bounds are separate from subtree bounds.
- **R2 Topic title:** 14px / 400, 19-unit baseline spacing, x=24 and y=`6 + font + i × line`; complete Topic rows remain in their trays. None of the flagged pairs is a Topic-row pair.
- **R3 Coverage:** `.category-coverage` is 10px / 400; x=22, baseline `card.height - 7`. It is a separate small metadata label within the owning Category card.
- **R4 Camera:** one `#world` translate/scale transform applies to all content. The same computed 17/21/28/14/10px fonts are retained in world units; there is no minimum font clamp, per-scope offset, semantic zoom, truncated name, hidden Topic or reorder.
- **R5 V6.6 optics:** `vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke` applies to cards, routes, core/ring and tray strokes; it does not enlarge text. Font weights, full label content and DOM inventory remain unchanged. The minimap/controls do not participate in these inside-card label pairs.

**Generic correction:** no implementation, CSS, packing or clearance change is warranted or made. The corrected *review measurement* uses transformed text envelopes as a broad-phase candidate test and actual glyph ink as its collision test, with independent natural-world/card/tray/routing checks. A font-cell envelope intersection alone is not a visible-collision assertion. The historical candidate's strict audit result is retained unchanged; this report resolves its interpretation rather than rewriting evidence or weakening semantic/world constraints.
